sentences.text: The fire exit is already drifting open.
You haul it shut, but it will not stay.
So you fetch the pallet jack.
One pallet of cat litter weighs nearly a ton.
You park four of them against the door.
Next, the staff entrance.
Eight employees hold a key to it.
You turn yours in the lock until it snaps off.
Now nobody has one.
If Rhea comes back, she will have to knock.
Emergency lamps are rated for two hours.
Long enough for everyone to walk out.
Nobody planned for somebody staying.
When they fade, you learn something about supermarkets.
They have no windows.
With the shutter down, you have built yourself a cave.
Aisle 9: flashlights and batteries.
You count those too.
Problem two: the rot.
Without power, a fridge keeps food safe for about five hours.
A full freezer, maybe three days.
After that, you are sealed in with three tons of meat, milk and fish.
But there is a walk-in freezer, a steel room with a rubber seal.
It was built to keep warm air out.
It keeps smells in just as well.
It takes you nine hours and a single cart.
You hold back the bread and the fruit.
For one week, you eat like a king.
Then you tape the seams and write on the door: house rule, nobody opens this, ever.
On the fourth morning, you climb onto the roof.
Three nights ago, the parking lot was empty.
Now there are 150 people standing in it.
All of them face the doors.
They are not hunting you.
They do not even know you are here.
It is Sunday morning.
They have come to do their shopping.
